description:
The behavioral-spec.md root-cause section frames the defect as generic/systemic ('deterministic, 100%-reproducible... on any machine where $HOME/.openclaw/.env exists and sets ANICCA_HOME, true for every instance colocated with the OpenClaw automaton on this Mac Mini') and the feature claims to fix 'the identity-resolution defect that caused the fail-closed path to trigger'. However, the fix touches ONLY skills/self/spawn/run.sh. Two other production skill wrappers contain the byte-identical, still-unfixed vulnerable preamble (set -a / source $HOME/.hermes/.env / source $HOME/.openclaw/.env / set +a with no ANICCA_HOME save-restore):

1. skills/economy/lending/run.sh:27-30 -- its own header comment (lines 2-5) explicitly states it is 'mirroring self/spawn/run.sh's own already-proven shape exactly', and it execs its own scripts/wake-gate.mjs identity-resolution entry point (line 32), the same pattern class that produced the original incident.
2. skills/self/spawn-child/run.sh:37-40 -- identical unpatched preamble.

Neither behavioral-spec.md's REQ-001 (scoped by name to only skills/self/spawn/run.sh) nor its 'Non-functional / safety constraints' section (lines 85-99) discloses, scopes out, or tracks these two sibling files as known-affected-but-out-of-scope. A reader of this spec would reasonably believe the identity-resolution defect class has been eliminated from the codebase; instead only one of at least three copies of the vulnerable preamble was patched, leaving a duplicated, unaddressed fragile/security-relevant code pattern in two other skills, one of which (economy/lending) is an active money-movement skill.

evidence.snippet:
# economy/lending/run.sh -- thin entrypoint ... mirroring self/spawn/run.sh's own already-proven shape exactly.
set -a
[ -f "$HOME/.hermes/.env" ]   && . "$HOME/.hermes/.env"
[ -f "$HOME/.openclaw/.env" ] && . "$HOME/.openclaw/.env"
set +a

exec "$NODE" "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/wake-gate.mjs" "$@"

additionalEvidence.snippet: This is a deterministic, 100%-reproducible bug, not a transient/race condition: it fires on every real (non-dry-run) invocation of self/spawn on any machine where $HOME/.openclaw/.env exists and sets ANICCA_HOME (true for every instance colocated with the OpenClaw automaton on this Mac Mini).

note: Confirmed economy/lending/scripts/wake-gate.mjs's current runWakeGate() does not itself read env.ANICCA_HOME for identity resolution (it resolves citizens via a shared registry lookup, and defaultDisburse expects deps.lenderPrivateKey to be injected rather than resolved via resolve-identity.mjs) -- so this specific sibling does not appear to CURRENTLY manifest the identical functional failure, but the vulnerable preamble is present verbatim and undocumented as a known residual risk, and self/spawn-child/run.sh has the same unpatched preamble as well. This is a live, uncontrolled duplication of a just-diagnosed defect pattern, not a hypothetical.
